title: Odd complete Bell networks have exact asymptotic GHZ cost k²/4
short: Exact entanglement cost of odd complete networks
plain: For any odd group of at least five participants, the claim determines the exact asymptotic quantum resource cost of creating entangled links between every pair, when success is allowed to be probabilistic.
who: OpenAI (2026), the stipulated exact rectangular exponent; Xiaohan Huang and Victor Y. Pan (1997), Fast Rectangular Matrix Multiplications and Improving Parallel Matrix Computations; Huanyi Zhou (2026), Asymptotic Rank of Weighted Graph Tensors via Completely Positive Bounds, arXiv:2610.34273v3; Matthias Christandl, Péter Vrana and Jeroen Zuiddam (2019), Asymptotic tensor rank of graph tensors: beyond matrix multiplication.
statement: Work over C. Fix an odd integer k≥5. Let Ψ_k consist of one independent qubit Bell pair between every pair of k parties, and let GHZ_k=(|0⟩^{⊗k}+|1⟩^{⊗k})/√2. Let h_k(N) be the minimum number of GHZ_k copies from which exact stochastic local operations and classical communication can prepare Ψ_k^{⊗N} with nonzero success probability, without additional shared entanglement. Then lim_{N→∞} h_k(N)/N=k²/4, equivalently h_k(N)=(k²/4)N+o(N). No uniform lower bound on the success probability is imposed. In tensor language, the equivalent new identity is log₂ R̃_C(GT₂(K_k))=k²/4.
derivation:
1. Write k=2m+1, so m≥2. The stipulated rectangular_exponent theorem states ω_C(x,y,z)=x+y+[max(0,(x+y)z−xy)]²/(4xyz) for x≥y≥z>0. Substituting (x,y,z)=(m²,m,m) gives s:=ω_C(m²,m,m)=m²+m+m⁴/(4m⁴)=k²/4. These weights meet every ordering and positivity hypothesis. [OpenAI, exact rectangular scope](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/main/lean/docs/107.md).

2. Set G=GT₂(K_k). Group its vertices into blocks of sizes m,m,1. Fix every internal edge label to zero. The remaining three-party tensor is B=⟨2^{m²},2^m,2^m⟩: there are m²,m,m edges between the respective blocks. This is precisely the construction in Zhou’s proof of Lemma 5.1, which states the inequality log₂ R̃_F(WT(Q_a))≤log₂ R̃_F(GT₂(K_A)), with (Q_a)_{ij}=2^{a_i a_j} and A=Σ_i a_i. Grouping preserves rank-one tensors, and the subsequent coordinate projections cannot increase rank; consequently R_C(B^{⊗N})≤R_C(G^{⊗N}) for every N. [Zhou, §5.1](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.34273v3#S5.SS1).

3. The arithmetic-to-rank transfer needs care. Huang–Pan, Definition 2.2, requires bilinear algorithms to compute identities in independent indeterminates; equation (2.3), with variables renamed, states A(a^t,b^t,c^t)=O(M(a,b,c)^t), where A counts arithmetic operations and M is minimum bilinear rank. Apply this to B^{⊗N}, whose dimensions are (2^{Nm²},2^{Nm},2^{Nm}), and write r_N=R_C(B^{⊗N}). Powering its bilinear algorithm and padding to the next block size gives ω_C(m²,m,m)≤log₂(r_N)/N. Explicitly, even the weaker recurrence C_t≤r_N C_{t−1}+O(2^{N(m²+m)(t−1)}) suffices: flattening gives r_N≥2^{N(m²+m)}, hence C_t=O(t r_N^t). This counts additions and multiplications and computes formal polynomial identities, exactly matching the stipulated model. Thus r_N≥2^{Ns}, and Step 2 gives log₂ R̃_C(G)≥s. [Huang–Pan, equation (2.3), p. 12](https://www.csd.uwo.ca/~mmorenom/CS855/Ressources/Huang-Pan-PASCO-1997.pdf).

4. Zhou’s Theorem 1.1 states, for every field F and integer k≥2, ⌊k²/4⌋≤log₂ R̃_F(GT₂(K_k))≤k²/4. Its upper bound applies over C. Together with Step 3, it proves log₂ R̃_C(G)=k²/4, closing the odd-k gap. [Zhou, Theorem 1.1](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.34273v3#S1.SS2).

5. Christandl–Vrana–Zuiddam, Proposition 1.19, states ω(ψ)=lim_{N→∞} N^{-1}log₂ R(ψ^{⊗N}); Definition 1.16 identifies this exponent with conversion from the rank-two GHZ tensor. The proposition’s proof gives the finite-copy cost h_k(N)=⌈log₂ R_C(G^{⊗N})⌉. Their introduction explicitly identifies G with independent EPR pairs between every pair of parties and the conversion with SLOCC. Normalizing these nonzero tensors does not change convertibility. Substituting Step 4 proves the stated preparation rate. [Published paper, Proposition 1.19, pp. 65–66, and p. 60](https://ir.cwi.nl/pub/28609/28609.pdf).
why_new: I read the supplied claim’s introduction, corollaries, §2.4, contents and bibliography, and checked its tensor-geometry companion’s introduction; none states this conclusion. Searches included 'odd complete graphs tensor exact', 'GT_2 K_5 25/4', 'complete graph tensors nine fourths', and 'GHZ complete graph 25/4'. No exact odd-k rank or preparation rate surfaced. Zhou’s November 11 version still leaves the quarter-unit gap, as does [Khoruzhii’s Theorem 3](https://lemmata.iol.berlin/tensor-rank). The new step closes that gap through the m,m,1 rectangular reduction, before invoking the quantum conversion theorem. For five parties it determines the rate as 25/4, sharpening the prior interval [6,25/4].
doubt: The conclusion uses the full exact rectangular formula stipulated from the Lean scope; the PDF’s square theorem and Corollary 1.3 alone do not establish it for every odd k. Zhou’s supporting upper bound is a public arXiv preprint, not a refereed publication. The novelty assessment is search-based, not an exhaustive priority guarantee.
